  <div><article id="task-template_cd5ff649-b94c-4546-82e9-6dac68310ab9" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h3>Create an autonomous AI agent</h3><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="">
      <p class="p">
        <div class="video-wrapper"><video controls="controls" autoplay="autoplay" loop="loop" muted="muted" src="https://cisco-api.ingeniuxondemand.com/DITA/content/en/us/td/i/400001-500000/480001-490000/488001-489000/488634.mp4" poster="https://cisco-api.ingeniuxondemand.com/DITA/content/en/us/td/i/400001-500000/480001-490000/488001-489000/488647.jpg" width="100%"></video></div>
      </p>
    </section><div class="section prereq p" id="prereq_kvr_kr1_f2c"><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p">Ensure to create the knowledge base for the autonomous AI agent. For more information, see
           <a data-scope="" href="#create-knowledge-source-for-ai-agent" target="" title="">Create knowledge source for AI agent</a>.</p>
    </div><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
        <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
          <p class="ph cmd" id="">Log in to the Webex AI Agent Studio platform.</p>
        </td></tr>
        <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
          <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <strong class="ph b">Dashboard</strong>, click <span class="ph uicontrol">+Create agent</span>.</p>
        </td></tr>
        <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
          <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Create an AI agent</span> screen, choose <span class="ph uicontrol">Start from
            scratch</span> and click <span class="ph uicontrol">Next</span>. </p>
          <div class="itemgroup info">
          <p class="p">
            <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 22 22" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M15.8125 2.75H6.1875C5.27615 2.75107 4.40243 3.11358 3.75801 3.75801C3.11358 4.40243 2.75107 5.27615 2.75 fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
              <p class="p">You can also choose a predefined template to create your AI agent quickly. You can
                filter the AI agent type as <code class="ph codeph">Autonomous</code>. In this case, the fields on
                the <strong class="ph b">Profile</strong> page autopopulate. For more information on the templates, see
                   <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n8mo4c/" target="_blank" title="">Use AI agent templates</a>.</p>
            </div></div></div></div>
          </p>
        </div>
        </td></tr>
        <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
          <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose <span class="ph uicontrol">Autonomous</span> agent type.</p>
        </td></tr>
        <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">5</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
          <p class="ph cmd" id="">Specify the following required details:</p>
          <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">Agent name</span>—Enter the name of the AI agent. The agent name
              can have a maximum length of 256 characters.</p>
            </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">System ID</span>—A system-generated unique identifier. This field
              is editable.</p>
            </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">AI engine</span>—Choose one of the following AI engines from the
              drop-down list to meet your contact center needs:</p>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Webex AI Pro 1.0 (to be deprecated soon)/ Webex AI Pro 2.0</span>:
                  This default option supports AI agents in multi-language contact centers,
                  delivering human-like conversations. </li><li class="li">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Webex AI Pro-US. 1.0 (to be deprecated soon)/Webex AI Pro-US.
                    2.0</span>: Delivers natural, human-like conversations in English, tailored
                  for US regional accents and regulatory requirements.<div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span                     <p class="p">Webex AI Pro-US 1.0/Webex AI Pro-US. 2.0 is available for US customers only.
                      Regional media from remote locations is currently not supported with this
                      engine.</p>
                  </div></div></div></div></li><li class="li">

13.5677 10.9276 13.3928 10.7986 13.2639C10.6697 13.1349 10.4948 13.0625 10.3125 13.0625Z" fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
                    <p class="p">Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0/Webex AI Pro-Europe 2.0 is available for EU customers
                      only. Regional media from remote locations is currently not supported with
                      this engine.</p>
                  </div></div></div></div></li></ul>
            </div>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
              <p class="p">Webex AI Pro 1.0, Webex AI Pro-US. 1.0, and Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0 will be
                deprecated in the near future.</p>
              <p class="p" />
            </div>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
              <p class="p">Your choice of AI engine determines the conversation settings—such as language,
                voice, DTMF, delays &amp; interruptions and vocabulary—available for configuring
                your AI agent. Since each engine offers unique capabilities, the configuration
                options displayed in the <strong class="ph b">Conversations</strong> tab will update dynamically based on
                your selection. For details about AI engine's capabilities, refer to the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/article/ne6s80cb" target="_blank" title="">Understand AI engines for AI agents</a> article. </p>
            </div>
            </li></ol>
        </td></tr>
        <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">6</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
          <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Create</span>. You've now successfully created the autonomous AI
          agent which is now available on the <span class="ph uicontrol">Dashboard</span>.</p>
          <div class="itemgroup info">
          <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22"             <p class="p">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li">You can create up to 100 AI agents, which include both scripted and autonomous
                  types.</li><li class="li"> Don’t create a single autonomous AI agent with a complex scope. Instead, create
                  multiple AI agents with limited scopes. Use the transfer action option to transfer
                  the call from one AI agent to another. See the   <a data-scope="" href="#concept-template_c583a7c5-84e6-43bf-a9a3-69d1855f1b08" target="" title="" /> section for more information.</li></ul>
            </p>
          </div></div></div></div>
        </div>
          <div class="itemgroup info">On the AI agent header, you can perform the following tasks:<ul class="ul"><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Preview</span></li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Copy Access Token</span></li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Delete</span></li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Export</span></li></ul>For more information, see  <a data-scope="" href="#section_us5_zdw_ycc" target="" title="">Tasks on AI agent card</a>.</div>
          <div class="itemgroup info">
          <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22"             <p class="p">You can also import prebuilt AI agents. For more information, see  <a data-scope="" href="#section_grn_byz_zcc" target="" title="">Import AI agent</a>.</p>
          </div></div></div></div>
        </div>
        </td></tr>
      </tbody></table><section class="section postreq" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">What to do next</p></div>
      <p class="p">Configure the autonomous AI agent.</p>
    </section></div></article></div>
  <div><article id="concept-template_44e053dc-5482-48e5-8b91-7f8aa7774fcd" class="topic concept "><h3>Configure autonomous AI agent</h3><div id="" class="body conbody">
      <p class="p">The following sections guide you on how to configure autonomous AI agent for your specific
        needs:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <p class="p"> <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_5416be2f-b95e-4b80-bebc-3fa8201414bf" target="" title="">Update autonomous AI agent profile</a></p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p"> <a data-scope="" href="#concept-template_5ea99e1f-a679-4cf9-8e33-7a4f83d9f66a" target="" title="">Add actions to autonomous AI agent</a></p>
          <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
              <p class="p"> <a data-scope="" href="#concept-template_0ec5103d-ff6f-426f-a28c-bb335bc7b1bb" target="" title="">Configure slot filling</a></p>
            </li><li class="li">
              <p class="p"> <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_74dc7494-8351-48cc-9e97-5ad6d0d52df6" target="" title="">Configure fulfillment</a></p>
            </li></ul>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p"> <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_9b7eb61b-facf-4467-902b-53276bd3723d" target="" title="">Configure knowledge base</a></p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p"> <a data-scope="" href="#configure_conversation_settings" target="" title="">Configure conversation
              settings</a></p>
        </li></ul></p>
    </div><div><article id="task-template_5416be2f-b95e-4b80-bebc-3fa8201414bf" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h4>Update autonomous AI agent profile</h4><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="">
      
      <p class="p">Use the <span class="ph uicontrol">Profile</span> tab to manage customer-facing identity settings.</p>
    </section><div class="section prereq p" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p">Create an autonomous AI agent.</p>
    </div><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Dashboard</span>, click the AI agent that you've created. </p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Navigate to the <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Configurations</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Profile</span></span> tab and configure the following details:</p>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">Agent name</span>—Edit the name of the AI agent, if needed.</p>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">System ID</span>—Edit the system id of the AI agent, if
              needed.</p>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">URL for agent profile image</span>—The default URL from where the
              system fetches the AI agent's logo or image. Change this if needed.</p>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">Time zone</span>—Displays the time zone configured at the organization
              level, by default. If needed, choose a different time zone for your individual AI
              agents from the drop-down list. </p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 22 22" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M15.8125 2.75H6.1875C5.27615 2.75107 4.40243 3.11358 3.75801 3.75801C3.11358 4.40243 2.75107 5.27615 2.75 fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
                <p class="p">The system preserves agent-level configurations when organization-level settings
                  change.</p>
              </div></div></div></div>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">AI engine</span>—Choose one of the following options from the
              drop-down list to update the AI engine:</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Webex AI Pro 1.0 (to be deprecated soon)/ Webex AI Pro 2.0</span>:
                  Supports AI agents in multi-language contact centers, delivering human-like
                  conversations. </li><li class="li">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Webex AI Pro-US. 1.0 (to be deprecated soon)/Webex AI Pro-US.
                    2.0</span>: Delivers natural, human-like conversations in English, tailored
                  for US regional accents and regulatory requirements. <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span                     <p class="p">Webex AI Pro-US 1.0//Webex AI Pro-US. 2.0 is available for US customers only.

                  </div></div></div></div></li><li class="li">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0 (to be deprecated soon)/Webex AI Pro-Europe

13.5677 10.9276 13.3928 10.7986 13.2639C10.6697 13.1349 10.4948 13.0625 10.3125 13.0625Z" fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
                    <p class="p">Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0/Webex AI Pro-Europe 2.0 is available for EU customers
                      only. </p>
                  </div></div></div></div></li></ul>
            </div>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <p class="p">Your choice of AI engine determines the conversation settings—such as language,
                voice, DTMF, delays &amp; interruptions and vocabulary—available for configuring
                your AI agent. Since each engine offers unique capabilities, the configuration
                options displayed in the <span class="ph uicontrol">Conversations</span> tab will update dynamically based on
                your selection. For details about AI engine's capabilities, refer to the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/article/ne6s80cb" target="_blank" title="">Understand AI engines for AI agents</a> article. </p>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
              <span class="ph uicontrol">AI transparency</span>—Enable or disable the transparency note that
              tells customers they are interacting with an AI agent. For new AI agents, the AI
              transparency toggle is enabled by default. If you turn it off, you must acknowledge
              the warning and provide a reason.</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <p class="p">
                <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">In European regions</strong>: This feature is enabled by default. A transparency
                    message plays or appears (depending on the channel) for all agent types. If
                    administrators decide to disable this feature, they must acknowledge the risks
                    and add audit comments before opting out.<div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span                       <p class="p">You can also configure AI transparency message for existing AI agents in
                        your organization. This is recommended but optional.</p>
                    </div></div></div></div></li></ul>
              </p>
            </div>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <p class="p">For voice conversations, a transparency note plays before the welcome message and
                callers cannot interrupt it. For digital conversations, the transparency note is
                added to the first AI-generated response in the session.</p>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">

                  message won't be automatically translated and will appear or play as configured,

          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Save changes</span>.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Publish</span> to make the AI agent live. For more information,
          see the  <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_bed3102a-f6bb-4ded-99d9-8ffb87f3dd9a" target="" title="">Publish your autonomous AI agent</a> section.</p>
          </td></tr>
        </tbody></table><section class="section postreq" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">What to do next</p></div>
      <p class="p">Define and optimize instructions for your Webex AI agent.</p>
    </section></div></article></div><div><article id="concept-template_b690286b-fda6-4794-8975-de53d27c6111" class="topic concept "><h4>AI-optimized instructions for autonomous agents</h4><div id="" class="body conbody">
        <p class="p">Webex AI Agent Studio provides AI-powered assistance to generate, optimize, and refine
      instructions for autonomous AI agents. Start from a simple description or example, improve
      existing instructions using prompt-engineering best practices, review the changes, and edit
      the result before saving. With this feature, you can create clear, well-structured
      instructions that maximize your AI agent's performance.</p>
        <section id="section_what_is_optimization" class="section">
      <h5 class="title sectiontitle">What is instruction optimization</h5>
      <p class="p">Instruction optimization is an AI-powered feature that analyzes your draft instructions and
        generates an improved version following best practices for LLM prompt engineering. The
        feature uses a specialized AI service to restructure your content into a format that Large
        Language Models understand most effectively.</p>
      <p class="p">The optimization process:</p>
      <ul class="ul"><li class="li">Analyzes your original instructions to understand intent and context.</li><li class="li">Applies proven LLM prompting patterns and structures.</li><li class="li">Generates instructions with clear sections for Role/Identity, Reasoning Order, Output
          Format, and Edge Cases, tailored to the selected AI engine. </li><li class="li">Provides a <span class="ph uicontrol">View changes</span> option so you can compare the original
          and AI-generated instructions side by side and review the highlighted changes.</li></ul>
    </section>
        <section id="section_when_to_use" class="section">
      <h5 class="title sectiontitle">When to use optimization</h5>
      <p class="p">Use the instruction optimization feature when:</p>
      <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <strong class="ph b">Creating a new agent</strong>: Start with a draft of your requirements and let the
          optimization feature structure them properly.</li><li class="li">
          <strong class="ph b">Improving existing agents</strong>: If your agent's responses are inconsistent or unclear,
          optimize the instructions to improve clarity.</li><li class="li">
          <strong class="ph b">Adapting to a new AI engine</strong>: When switching between AI engines (e.g., from Webex AI
          Pro 1.0 to Webex AI Pro-US 1.0), re-optimize instructions to align with the new model's
          capabilities.</li></ul>
      <p class="p">Review the optimized version alongside your original to ensure that the instructions are
        accurate.</p>
    </section>
        <section id="section_limitations" class="section">
      <h5 class="title sectiontitle">Limitations and considerations</h5>
      <p class="p">Be aware of the following limitations when using instruction optimization:</p>
      <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">Stateless operation</strong>:Each optimization request is independent. To refine the
          result, edit the instructions or add follow-up guidance, then run the optimization again. </li><li class="li">
          <strong class="ph b">Design-time only</strong>: Optimization is available only when configuring an agent, not for
          runtime adjustments.</li><li class="li">
          <strong class="ph b">Manual review required</strong>: Always review optimized instructions to ensure they include
          your specific business context, terminology, and requirements.</li><li class="li">
          <strong class="ph b">Network dependency</strong>: Requires an active connection to the optimization service;
          offline editing is not optimized.</li></ul>
    </section>
      </div><div><article id="task-template_2285157c-d0fa-41d9-98b4-9082d7a33c9e" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h5>Define and optimize instructions</h5><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="">
      <p class="p">Use instruction optimization to improve draft instructions before you save or publish the
        AI agent.</p>
    </section><div class="section prereq p" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p"> Create an autonomous AI agent.</p>
    </div><table class="stepTable" id="steps_s5h_b5z_1kc" border="0"><tbody>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Dashboard</span> click the autonomous AI agent that you have
          created.</p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Navigate to <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Configuration</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Instructions</span></span> tab.</p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Enter draft instructions for your AI agent with a short description of the Agent's goal
          and expected behavior. </p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Alternatively, navigate to the <strong class="ph b">Examples</strong> tab, choose an example, and click
            <strong class="ph b">Insert example</strong>. </p>

        </div>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">5</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Optimize instruction</span> after drafting the instructions. Wait

14.4375H10.3125C10.4948 14.4375 10.6697 14.3651 10.7986 14.2361C10.9276 14.1072 11 13.9323 11 13.75C11 13.5677 10.9276 13.3928 10.7986 13.2639C10.6697 13.1349 10.4948 13.0625 10.3125 13.0625Z" fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
            <p class="p">Optimization feature handles non-sensical instructions and also refines abusive,
              offensive or overly strong language.</p>
          </div></div></div></div>
        </div>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">7</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">After reviewing optimized instructions, you can provide feedback. Under <strong class="ph b">Is this
            helpful?</strong>, select thumbs up or thumbs down to rate the AI-generated instructions.
        </p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">8</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Save changes</span>.</p>
            </td></tr>
          </tbody></table><section class="section postreq" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">What to do next</p></div>
      <p class="p"> Configure actions for your autonomous AI Agent.</p>
    </section></div></article></div></article></div><div><article id="concept-template_5ea99e1f-a679-4cf9-8e33-7a4f83d9f66a" class="topic concept "><h4>Add actions to autonomous AI agent </h4><div id="" class="body conbody">
        <p class="p">Autonomous AI agents are designed to comprehend user intents and act accordingly. For
      example, consider a restaurant with the need to automate online food order intake. To
      accomplish the task, create an autonomous AI agent that performs the following actions: <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Get the required information from the customer.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Transfer the information to the required flow.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Deliver the customer requirement.</p>
        </li></ul></p>
        <p class="p">The autonomous AI agent works on the following three building blocks:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Action—A task that an AI agent performs by understanding user intents and completes by
            connecting to external systems. </p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Entity or slot—Represents a step in fulfilling the user's intent. Slot filling involves
            asking specific questions to the customer to fulfill the customer's intent based on
            utterances. It's the trigger for an AI agent to start performing an action.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Fulfillment—Determines how the AI agent completes the action by connecting with
            external systems.</p>
        </li></ul></p>
      </div><div><article id="task-template_031f8a5e-98ec-4521-ad2f-6c271e5a969b" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="context_apg_n2f_53c" /><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Dashboard</span>, click the AI agent that you've created.</p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Navigate to <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Configurations</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Actions</span></span> tab.</p>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
          <p class="p">The <span class="ph uicontrol">Actions</span> page displays the <strong class="ph b">Agent handover</strong> action. The
              <span class="ph uicontrol">Agent handover</span> action is enabled by default allowing the AI
            agent to escalate the conversation to a human agent. Use the toggle option to disable
            it.</p>
        </div>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">+Add Actions</span> to add a new action for an AI agent.</p>
              <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                  <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Browse actions</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Select available</span></span> for MCP client configuration. </p>
                </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                  <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Add new</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Fulfillment</span></span> to create fulfillment action.</p>
                </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                  <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Add new</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Transfer</span></span> to create a custom transfer action.</p>
                </li></ol>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
          <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 22 22" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M15.8125 2.75H6.1875C5.27615 2.75107 4.40243 3.11358 3.75801 3.75801C3.11358 4.40243 2.75107 5.27615 2.75 fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
            <p class="p">You can configure a maximum of 10 actions for an AI agent.</p>
          </div></div></div></div>
        </div>
              <div class="itemgroup info">See the following sections for detailed configuration steps.</div>
            </td></tr>
          </tbody></table></div></article></div></article></div><div><article id="task-template_74dc7494-8351-48cc-9e97-5ad6d0d52df6" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h4>Configure fulfillment</h4><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="context_ez5_tbn_g2c">
      <p class="p">You can configure fulfillment flows for AI agent actions on the Webex Connect Flow builder.
        For more information, see  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webexconnect.io/docs/configure-fulfilment-flows-for-ai-agent-actions" target="_blank" title=""><u>Configure Fulfillment Flows for AI Agent
          Actions</u></a>.</p>
      <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 22 22" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M15.8125 2.75H6.1875C5.27615 2.75107 4.40243 3.11358 3.75801 3.75801C3.11358 4.40243 2.75107 5.27615 2.75         <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
            <p class="p">As part of PCI compliance, autonomous AI agent currently doesn't support fulfillment
              that involves debit card or credit cards. All user verification or payment that
              involve a debit card or credit card must be done through third-party integration.</p>
          </li></ul>
      </div></div></div></div>
    </section><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Add a new action</span> page, specify the following
          details:</p>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Action name</span>—Enter the name of the action. For example,
                <code class="ph codeph">Book tickets</code>. The maximum length of the <span class="ph uicontrol">Action
                name</span> field is 64 characters.</p>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                  <span class="ph uicontrol">Action description</span>—Provide a brief description about the
              expected action. Ensure that the action description is clear and accurate. The maximum
              length of <span class="ph uicontrol">Action description</span> is 1024 characters.</p>
              </li></ol>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Configure slots. See the  <a data-scope="" href="#concept-template_0ec5103d-ff6f-426f-a28c-bb335bc7b1bb" target="" title="">Configure slot filling</a> for more
          information.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Configure fulfillment. You can choose one of the following options.</p>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">If you choose <span class="ph uicontrol">Use Webex Connect Flow Builder Fulfillment</span>,
              perform the following configuration:</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Select service</span>—Choose the required service that is
                  configured in the Webex Connect client workspace.<div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 22 22" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M15.8125 2.75H6.1875C5.27615 2.75107 4.40243 3.11358                     <p class="p">The Webex AI Agent Studio can only access service and flows configured within
                      the client-level workspace.</p>
                  </div></div></div></div></li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Select a flow</span>—Choose the required flow that is configured
                  in the Webex Connect client workspace.</li></ul>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">If you choose, <span class="ph uicontrol">Manage in the source flow (voice only)</span>, you
              must configure custom events. See the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5uo60x/Configure-custom-data-and-custom-events-for-AI-agents" target="_blank" title="">Configure custom data and custom events for AI
                agents</a> for detailed information.</p>
              </li></ol>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Add</span> to complete the configuration.</p>
          </td></tr>
        </tbody></table><section class="section postreq" id="postreq_i3y_q2r_bdc"><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">What to do next</p></div>
      <p class="p">Configure the knowledge base.</p>
    </section></div><div><article id="concept-template_0ec5103d-ff6f-426f-a28c-bb335bc7b1bb" class="topic concept "><h5>Configure slot filling</h5><div id="" class="body conbody">
          <p class="p">Slot filling involves adding the required input entities for the AI engine. In the
        <span class="ph uicontrol">Slot filling</span> section of the <span class="ph uicontrol">Actions</span> page, add
      the input entities:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <p class="p"> You can add the entities one by one in table format. For more information, see  <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_9848e5ed-72de-4e31-a88d-e7a0b141399a" target="" title="">Add input entities in table format</a>.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">You can also use the JSON file and define the entities. See  <a data-scope="external" href="https://tour.json-schema.org/" target="_blank" title="">A Tour of JSON
              Schema</a> for details.</p>
        </li></ul></p>
        </div><div><article id="task-template_9848e5ed-72de-4e31-a88d-e7a0b141399a" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h6>Add input entities in table format</h6><div id="" class="body taskbody">
            <table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
              <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">To add an input entity, click <strong class="ph b">+New input entity</strong>. </p>
              </td></tr>
              <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Add a new input entity</span> page, specify the following
          details:</p>
                <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                    <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                      <span class="ph uicontrol">Entity name</span>—Enter the name of the input entity. The maximum
              length of the <span class="ph uicontrol">Entity name</span> can be 256 characters.</p>
                  </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                    <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                      <span class="ph uicontrol">Entity type</span>—Choose the data type of the entity.</p>
                  </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                    <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                      <span class="ph uicontrol">Entity description</span>—Provide a brief description about the
              entity. Ensure that the entity description is clear and accurate. The maximum length
              of the <span class="ph uicontrol">Entity description</span> can be 512 characters.</p>
                  </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                    <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                      <span class="ph uicontrol">Entity examples</span>—Enter an example for the entity. Click
                <span class="ph uicontrol">+Add</span> to add more examples.</p>
                  </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                    <p class="ph cmd" id="">Check the <span class="ph uicontrol">Required</span> check box to make this entity
              mandatory.</p>
                  </li></ol>
              </td></tr>
              <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Add</span> to add the input entity. You can add as many input
          entities as you need.</p>
              </td></tr>
              <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Add</span> to add the action to the AI agent.</p>
              </td></tr>
              <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">5</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Publish</span> to make the AI Agent live. For more information,
          see the  <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_bed3102a-f6bb-4ded-99d9-8ffb87f3dd9a" target="" title="">Publish your autonomous AI agent</a>.</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
          <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22"             <p class="p">After adding the action, use the <strong class="ph b">Controls</strong> option to edit or delete the

        </div>
              </td></tr>
            </tbody></table>
          </div></article></div><div><article id="concept-template_7d93102d-6315-44a3-a257-9c211827de36" class="topic concept "><h6>Add entities using a JSON editor</h6><div id="" class="body conbody">
            <p class="p">
      <ol class=""><li class="li">To add an input entity in JSON, click <span class="ph uicontrol">Use JSON instead</span>.</li><li class="li">Enter the input parameter schema in JSON format.</li><li class="li">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Add</span>.</li></ol>
    </p>
            <p class="p">For more information, see  <a data-scope="external" href="https://tour.json-schema.org/" target="_blank" title="">A Tour of JSON Schema.</a></p>
            <section id="section_c22_vkp_bdc" class="section">
      <p><strong class="ph b">Input parameter structure</strong></p>
      <p class="p">The input parameters must adhere to the following structure:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
            <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">type</strong>—Data type of the parameters object. This is always 'object' to denote
              that the parameters are structured as an object.</p>
            <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">properties</strong>—An object where each key represents a parameter and its associated
              metadata.</p>
            <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">required</strong>—An array of strings listing the names of parameters that are
              mandatory.</p>
          </li></ul></p>
    </section>
            <section id="section_xfv_qht_bdc" class="section">
      <p><strong class="ph b">properties Object</strong></p>
      <p class="p">Each key in the <strong class="ph b">properties object</strong> represents an input entity/parameter and contains
        another object with metadata about that parameter. The metadata should always include the
        following keywords:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
            <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">type</strong>—Data type of the parameter. The allowed types are:</p>
            <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
                <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">string</strong>—Textual data.</p>
              </li><li class="li">
                <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">integer</strong>—Numeric data without decimals.</p>
              </li><li class="li">
                <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">number</strong>—Numeric data that can include decimals.</p>
              </li><li class="li">
                <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">boolean</strong>—True/false values.</p>
              </li><li class="li">
                <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">array</strong>—A list of items, all of which are typically of the same type.</p>
              </li><li class="li">
                <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">object</strong>—A complex data structure with nested properties.</p>
              </li></ul>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">description</strong>—A brief explanation of what the entity represents. This helps the
              AI engine understand the purpose and usage of the parameter. A description that's
              concise and consistent with the agent's instructions and action description is good
              for better accuracy.</p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">Validation is enforced by the platform for ‘type’ only. ‘Description’ isn't enforced
              for all entities but it's highly recommended that it’s added. Other useful keywords
              for entity metadata are:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
                  <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">enum</strong>—The enum field lists the possible values for a parameter. This is
                    useful for parameters that should only accept a limited set of values.
                    Developers can define custom lists of values that a parameter should accept to
                    use this.</p>
                </li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">pattern</strong>—Use the pattern field with string types to specify a regular
                  expression that the string must match. This is useful for validating specific
                  formats, such as phone numbers, postal codes, or custom identifiers.</li><li class="li">
                  <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">examples</strong>—The examples field provides one or more examples of valid
                    values for the parameter. This helps the AI engine understand the kind of data
                    it needs and can be especially useful for interpretation and validation
                    purposes.</p>
                </li></ul></p>
          </li></ul></p>
      <p class="p">There are other keywords that can make the entity definition more accurate and robust. For
        more information, see  <a data-scope="external" href="https://tour.json-schema.org/" target="_blank" title="">A Tour of JSON Schema</a>.</p>
    </section>
            <section id="section_rjw_fnp_bdc" class="section">
      <p><strong class="ph b">Example</strong></p>
      <p class="p">The following example includes various types of entities and keywords:</p>
      <pre class="codeblock"><code class="codeblock">The following example includes various types of entities and keywords:

{
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "username": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The unique username for the account.",
            "minLength": 3,
            "maxLength": 20
        },
        "password": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The password for the account.",
            "minLength": 8,
            "format": "password"
        },
        "email": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The email address for the account.",
            "pattern": "\\w+([-+.']\\w+)*@\\w+([-.]\\w+)*\\.\\w+([-.]\\w+)*"
        },
        "birthdate": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The birthdate of the user.",
            "examples": ["mm/dd/YYYY"]
        },
        "preferences": {
            "type": "object",
            "description": "User preferences settings.",
            "properties": {
                "newsletter": {
                    "type": "boolean",
                    "description": "Whether the user wants to receive newsletters.",
                    "default": true
                },
                "notifications": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "Preferred notification method.",
                    "enum": ["email", "sms", "push"]
                }
            }
        },
        "roles": {
            "type": "array",
            "description": "List of roles assigned to the user.",
            "items": {
                "type": "string",
                "enum": ["user", "admin", "moderator"]
            }
        }
    },
    "required": ["username", "password", "email"]
}</code></pre>
      <p class="p">This example includes the following entities:<ul class="ul"><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">username</strong>—A string type with minimum and maximum length constraint.</li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">password</strong>—A string type with a minimum length and a specific format (password
            indicates that secure handling is required).</li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">email</strong>—A string type with a regex pattern to ensure it’s a valid email
            address.</li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">birthdate</strong>—A string type with examples to prescribe the format of the date.</li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">preferences</strong>—An object type with nested properties (newsletter and
            notifications), including a boolean with a default value and a string with specific
            allowed values (enum).</li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">roles</strong>—An array type where each item is a string limited to specific values
              (enum).<div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 22 22" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M15.8125 2.75H6.1875C5.27615 2.75107 4.40243 3.11358 3.75801 3.75801C3.11358 4.40243 2.75107 5.27615 2.75 14.4375H10.3125C10.4948 14.4375 10.6697 14.3651 10.7986 14.2361C10.9276 14.1072 11 13.9323 11 13.75C11 13.5677 10.9276 13.3928 10.7986 13.2639C10.6697 13.1349 10.4948 13.0625 10.3125 13.0625Z" fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
              <p class="p">The username, password, and email are mandatory as defined by the ‘required’
                array.</p>
            </div></div></div></div></li></ul></p>
      <p class="p">In this example, the entities have descriptive names, clear descriptions, and follow a
        consistent structure and naming convention. Follow these best practices to create
        well-defined entities that are easy for the AI engine to interpret and enforce.</p>
      <p class="p">This schema will result in JSON format being sent to connect AI Agent start node that looks
        like the following:<pre class="codeblock"><code class="codeblock">{
    "username":"username-example",
    "password":"password-example",
    "email":"fake@example.com",
    "preferences": {
        "newsletter":true,
        "notifications":"email, sms"
    },
    "roles":"user"
    
}</code></pre></p>
      <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22"         <p class="p">Webex Connect might not receive the preferences and roles input in certain situations
          because they were not designated as required in the schema.</p>
      </div></div></div></div>
    </section>
          </div></article></div></article></div></article></div><div><article id="concept-template_9483e1f4-c3e2-4080-b9d3-5359b553a785" class="topic concept "><h4>Configure MCP client action</h4><div id="" class="body conbody">
        <p class="p">The Model Context Protocol (MCP) client capability enables the autonomous AI agents to
      connect directly to third-party tools and services without requiring custom-built API
      integrations. This streamlines how agents retrieve data and perform actions during live
      customer conversations.</p>
        <p class="p">By setting up an MCP client, your AI agents can:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">Automatically invoke third-party tools during live conversations.</li><li class="li">Retrieve real-time data from external systems.</li><li class="li">Perform actions without human intervention.</li></ul></p>
      </div><div><article id="task-template_c15af56d-160d-4a6b-bd14-1560595b73e3" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="" /><div class="section prereq p" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p">Before you configure MCP action in the Webex AI Agent Studio, you must:</p>
      <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Have the MCP server URL, authentication type, and credentials for the third-party tools
            you want to connect.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Register MCP apps on the Webex Developer Portal. See the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://developer.webex.com/mcp/docs/onboard-your-agent" target="_blank" title="">Onboard your Agent App</a> section in the developer portal for
            more information. The Webex AI Agent studio supports only the following authentication
            types:              :<ul class="ul"><li class="li">OAuth2 client credentials</li><li class="li">API key</li><li class="li">Custom Header based Auth</li></ul></p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Authorize the tool in the Control Hub for your organization. See the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://developer.webex.com/mcp/docs/provisioning-on-control-hub" target="_blank" title="">Provision on Control Hub</a> section in the developer portal for
            more information.</p>
        </li></ul>
      <p class="p">
        <strong class="ph b">Note:</strong> MCP actions are read-only once created. If you need to change action settings,
        you must create a new action.</p>
    </div><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Log in to the Webex AI Agent Studio platform.</p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose the AI agent for which you want to configure the MCP action. You can also create
          a new autonomous AI agent. See  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/preview/ncs9r37/Webex-AI-Agent-Studio-Administration-guide#task-template_cd5ff649-b94c-4546-82e9-6dac68310ab9" target="_blank" title="">Create an autonomous AI agent</a> section for more
          information.</p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Navigate to the <span class="ph uicontrol">Actions</span> tab. Click <span class="ph uicontrol">+Add
            actions</span>.</p>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">In the <span class="ph uicontrol">Add actions</span> pop-up, under <span class="ph uicontrol">Browse
            actions</span> choose <span class="ph uicontrol">Select available</span></p>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
          <p class="p">This displays all the available MCP tools with the provider name and MCP label.</p>
        </div>
            </td></tr>
            <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">5</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
              <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose the MCP tool you want to add. You can add multiple MCP tools at any time. Click
            <span class="ph uicontrol">Add</span>.</p>
              <div class="itemgroup info">
          <p class="p">Your agent can support a maximum number of actions as defined by your organization's
            configuration. </p>
        </div>
            </td></tr>
          </tbody></table><section class="section postreq" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">What to do next</p></div>
      <p class="p">Once an MCP tool is added, the system automatically populates the following details from
        the MCP server definition:</p>
      <p class="p">
        <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">Action name (MCP tool name)</strong></li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">Description</strong></li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">Input entities</strong> (required fields and data types) </li></ul>
      </p>
      <p class="p">If you need to modify any of these details, you must update the MCP server definition at
        the registration or provisioning stage. Changes get synchronized automatically to the AI
        Agent Studio via notifications.</p>
      <p class="p"><strong class="ph b">Verify MCP tool status</strong></p>
      <p class="p">After adding an MCP action, verify its status in the action list:<ul class="ul"><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Tool name, description, and server details</strong>
            </p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Input parameters</strong> sent to the tool</p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Output</strong> returned by the tool</p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Execution state</strong> (Success or Failure)</p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Latency</strong> (in milliseconds)</p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Server name and ID</strong>
            </p>
          </li><li class="li">
            <p class="p">
              <strong class="ph b">Transaction ID</strong>
            </p>
          </li></ul></p>
      <p class="p">
        <strong class="ph b">Limitations</strong>
      </p>
      <p class="p">Be aware of the following limitations:</p>
      <ul class="ul"><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Group-level access control is not supported. MCP tool access is managed at the
            organization level only.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">MCP actions are read-only once created in AI Agent Studio. To update an action, create
            a new one.</p>
        </li><li class="li">
          <p class="p">Maximum number of actions per agent is defined by your organization's configuration.
            Contact your administrator for details.</p>
        </li></ul>
    </section></div></article></div></article></div><div><article id="task-template_91018ba5-7914-4ad9-938f-f8837f776f8c" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h4>Configure custom transfer action</h4><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="">
      <p class="p">The custom transfer action feature enables you to transfer calls from one AI agent to
        another AI agent, to a human agent, or to any another desired destination (voicemail box,
        hunt group, or any other number) to ensure seamless customer experience. Depending on the
        need, you can configure the transfer as an announced transfer or a silent transfer. By using
        a transfer action, you exit out of the escalated path of the Virtual Agent V2 Activity in
        Flow Builder with metadata that allows you to orchestrate the next path in the conversation.
        See the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/5a07xcb/Multi-agent-orchestration" target="_blank" title="">Multi-agent orchestration</a> article for more details
        on flow configuration.</p>
      
    </section><div class="section prereq p" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p">Create the required autonomous AI agents to use when transferring calls. You can now
        configure each transfer action independently.</p>
    </div><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Dashboard</span>, click the AI agent that you've created.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Navigate to <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Configurations</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Actions</span></span> tab.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click the <span class="ph uicontrol">Create new</span> drop-down list.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Create a transfer action</span> page, specify the following
          details:</p>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">In the <span class="ph uicontrol">General information</span> section, specify the following
              details:</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Action name</span>—Enter the name of the action. For example,
                  Leave_Voicemail.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Transfer condition</span>—Describe the condition for transfer.
                  For example, the user wants to leave a voicemail.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Transfer visibility</span>—Toggle option to announce
                    transfers.<ul class="ul"><li class="li">Turn-on the toggle: the AI Agent informs the customer about the transfer
                      before executing it.</li><li class="li">Turn off the toggle: the AI Agent performs a silent transfer and handles the
                      action using neutral languages.</li></ul>
                </li></ul>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">(optional) Click <span class="ph uicontrol">+New input entity</span>. In the <span class="ph uicontrol">Add a
                new input entity</span> page, enter the following details:</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Entity name</span>—Enter the name of the input entity. The
                  maximum length of the Entity name can be 256 characters.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Entity type</span>—Choose the data type of the entity.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Entity description</span>—Provide a brief description about the
                  entity. Ensure that the entity description is clear and accurate. The maximum
                  length of the Entity description can be 512 characters.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Entity examples</span>—Enter an example for the entity. Click
                  +Add to add more examples.</li></ul>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Add</span>.</p>
              </li></ol>
          </td></tr>
        </tbody></table><section class="section postreq" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">What to do next</p></div>Configure the Virtual Agent V2 activity. See the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/s0qro1/Use-AI-agents-for-customer-interactions" target="_blank" title="">Use AI agents for customer interactions</a> for more
      details.</section></div></article></div><div><article id="task-template_9b7eb61b-facf-4467-902b-53276bd3723d" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h4>Configure knowledge base</h4><div id="" class="body taskbody">
        <div class="section prereq p" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p">Create an autonomous AI agent.</p>
    </div>
        <table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <span class="ph uicontrol">Dashboard</span> page, click the AI agent that you've
          created.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Navigate to the <span class="menucascade"><span class="ph uicontrol">Configurations</span> &gt; <span class="ph uicontrol">Knowledge </span></span> tab.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Choose the required knowledge base from the drop-down list. </p>
            <div class="itemgroup info">
          <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22" fill="#1170CF" /></svg></span>
            <p class="p">We strongly recommend you to choose a knowledge base that uses the same language as
              your AI agent for optimal performance.</p>
          </div></div></div></div>
        </div>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">To navigate to the chosen <span class="ph uicontrol">Knowledge base</span>, choose
                <span class="ph uicontrol">Manage Knowledge base</span> from the drop-down list.</p>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">To disconnect the knowledge base from the AI agent, choose
                <span class="ph uicontrol">None</span> from the drop-down list.</p>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">To create a new knowledge base, choose <span class="ph uicontrol">+Add New</span> from the
              drop-down list. For more information, see  <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_81b96f90-1e6b-4e42-9cc1-c0d2c70f2f7c" target="" title="">Create knowledge base for AI agent</a>.</p>
              </li></ol>
            <div class="itemgroup info">
          <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22"             <p class="p">You can map a knowledge base to multiple AI agents.</p>
          </div></div></div></div>
        </div>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Save changes</span>.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">5</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Click <span class="ph uicontrol">Publish</span> to make the AI agent live. For more information,
          see  <a data-scope="" href="#task-template_bed3102a-f6bb-4ded-99d9-8ffb87f3dd9a" target="" title="">Publish your autonomous AI agent</a>.</p>
          </td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
      </div></article></div><div><article id="configure_conversation_settings" class="topic task no_summary_steps"><h4>
        <strong class="ph b">Configure conversation settings</strong>
      </h4><div id="" class="body taskbody"><section class="section context" id="">
      <p class="p">This section outlines how to configure the AI agent’s language and voice, choose a response
        style, add custom words for recognition, and manage how the AI agent handles pauses or
        interruptions during conversations. </p>
    </section><div class="section prereq p" id=""><div class="tasklabel"><p font-weight="bold" class="sectiontitle tasklabel cB_Bold">Before you begin</p></div>
      <p class="p">
        <ul class="ul"><li class="li">Ensure you are logged into the Webex AI Agent Studio.</li><li class="li">Ensure you’ve created the autonomous AI agent.</li></ul>
      </p>
    </div><table class="stepTable" id="" border="0"><tbody>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">1</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the <strong class="ph b">Dashboard</strong> page, click the AI agent that you've created.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">2</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">On the AI agent configuration page, navigate to the <strong class="ph b">Configuration </strong>&gt;
            <strong class="ph b">Conversation</strong> tab.</p>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">3</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Configure the <strong class="ph b">Language and response style </strong>settings:</p>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                  <strong class="ph b">Language: </strong>Based on the chosen AI engine for your AI agent (while creating
              the agent or updating the AI agent profile), configure the required language
              option:</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li">For the <i>Webex AI Pro 1.0</i> engine, the default language is set to
                    <code class="ph codeph">English</code>. Choose the desired language from the drop-down list.
                  To view the list of supported languages, see the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/pdef2d/Supported-languages-for-Scripted-AI-Agents" target="_blank" title="">Supported languages and voices</a>
                  article.</li><li class="li">For the <i>Webex AI Pro-US 1.0</i> engine, <i>English</i> is the only supported
                  language by default, with <code class="ph codeph">en-US</code> set as the default locale.
                    <i>Webex AI Pro-US 1.0</i> is available for US customers only.</li><li class="li">For the <i>Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0</i> engine, <i>English</i> is the only
                  supported language by default, with <code class="ph codeph">en-GB</code> set as the default
                  locale. <i>Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0</i> is available for Europe customers
                  only.</li></ul>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                  <strong class="ph b">Response style: </strong>—Choose how you want your AI agent to respond to
              customers:</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">Active</strong>
                  <strong class="ph b">- quick acknowledgments before a substantive response</strong>—Provides quick
                  acknowledgments before giving a full response. This means the agent will first say
                  something like "I understand your response" or "Got it," which helps reassure the
                  customer that their input was received before moving on to a detailed answer. You
                  can further configure style, frequency, and length of the responses:<ul class="ul"><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Style</span>—Choose the response style for the conversation:
                        <span class="ph uicontrol">Brief</span>, <span class="ph uicontrol">Empathetic</span>,
                        <span class="ph uicontrol">Conversational</span>, or <span class="ph uicontrol">Formal</span>. For
                      example, conversations in a healthcare setting should use an empathetic tone. </li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Frequency</span>—Choose an appropriate response frequency:
                        <span class="ph uicontrol">Always</span> or <span class="ph uicontrol">When appropriate</span>.
                      Too many responses can sometimes be distracting or annoying.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Length</span>—Choose the preferred response length:<ul class="ul"><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Very short</span>: Up to two words.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Short</span>: Up to four words.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Medium</span>: Up to six words.</li><li class="li"><span class="ph uicontrol">Long</span>: Up to eight words.</li></ul></li></ul></li><li class="li"><strong class="ph b">Direct - slight delay, only returns the substantive response</strong>—The agent
                  waits for a moment and then replies with only the substantive response, without
                  any initial acknowledgment.</li><li class="li">Check the <strong class="ph b">Include disfluencies</strong> check box if you want to add fillers like
                  "um" or "like" to make the agent sound more human and relatable.</li></ul>
              
            </div>
              </li></ol>
          </td></tr>
          <tr class="li step" id=""><td align="center" valign="middle" class="ordered-number">4</td><td align="left" valign="top" border="0">
            <p class="ph cmd" id="">Configure the <strong class="ph b">Voice channel </strong>settings:</p>
            <ol type="a" class="ol substeps"><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                  <strong class="ph b">Voice</strong>—Choose the desired voice for your AI agent from the <strong class="ph b">Select
                voice</strong> drop-down, based on the chosen AI engine and configured language. To view
              the list of supported voices, see the  <a data-scope="external" href="https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/pdef2d/Supported-languages-for-Scripted-AI-Agents" target="_blank" title="">Supported languages and voices</a> article.</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <ul class="ul"><li class="li">For the <i>Webex AI Pro 1.0</i> engine, the default voice for English is
                    <code class="ph codeph">en-US-Jennifer</code>. To use a different language or voice, select
                  the preferred language in the previous step; the available voices for that
                  language will then appear in the drop-down. </li><li class="li">For the <i>Webex AI Pro-US 1.0</i> engine, the default voice for English is set
                  to <code class="ph codeph">en-US-Jess</code>. Currently, you can only switch to other English
                  voices. </li><li class="li">
                  <p class="p">For the <i>Webex AI Pro-Europe 1.0</i> engine, the default voice for English is
                    set to <code class="ph codeph">en-GB-Grace</code>. Currently, you can switch to
                      <code class="ph codeph">en-IE</code> voices only. </p>
                </li></ul>
            </div>
              </li><li class="li substep substepexpand">
                <p class="ph cmd" id="">
                  <strong class="ph b">Speaking rate</strong>—Enter the numeric value to increase or decrease the rate/speed
              of speech output. Valid values range from 0.7 to 1.2, with the default set to 1.0 for
              normal speed.</p>
                <div class="itemgroup info">
              <div class="olh_note"><div class="note__content"><div class="olh_note" role="note"><div class="note-container"><span class="svg-container"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="22" height="22"
